correctness.rationale: For 1/2<p<1, 0<q<1/2, 0<w<1 and n=2m+1, conditionally iid within one common latent two-state environment gives the binomial-increment identity ΔB_m(t)=C(2m+1,m)(2t-1)[t(1-t)]^(m+1). Thus sign(J_(m+1)-J_m)=sign(R-z^m) with R=w(2p-1)s_p/[(1-w)(1-2q)s_q] and z=s_q/s_p. z>1 yields a unique peak or an adjacent tie at integral log(R)/log(z); z<1 yields at most a trough and its finite/global supremum is max{J0,w}, attained only at n=1 when J0>=w; z=1 yields monotone or constant behavior. Fixed 0<q<1/2,w>1/2 as p→1-q+ gives n_opt ~ [2q(1-q)/(1-2q)] log(w/(1-w))/(p+q-1). Independent exact Fraction checks re-derived 252 increments and the rational J0,J1,J2 witness. The analytic sign argument, not finite tests, proves unbounded n.
